units.scope: self-check distractor quality across the curriculum
units.detail: LENGTH_TELL 21 -> 0; the editorial audit reports ok:true for the first time. A full scan found 155 tell-questions across 49 sections, of which 60 were false positives where the options are artifacts (commit messages, commands) and being longer is being right. The detector now excludes those and names the real defect, explanatory asymmetry. ~230 distractors rewritten as misconceptions a learner could hold; nothing padded. S31 was the worst: every distractor was an ethical strawman, so the answer was readable from tone without touching the content.

units.scope: Phase E widened from one section to all 52
units.detail: scripts/phase_e_packet_sweep.py builds the cumulative learner packet for every active section and asserts the firewall on the shape the builder really emits: selfCheck_stems present with options and no correctIndex/answer/explanation; weDo present with starterCode but no solutionCode and no hint; prior == index-1; stable packet hash. Each withholding assertion is paired with a positive one so the check cannot pass by the learner receiving nothing, and a negative control plants a leak so a green result proves the gate can go red. 52 sections, 0 leaks, control true. This is harness validation, NOT a learner journey and NOT independent human review.
